deck.request: Where should Lumen invest next to hold its lead over Quill and Paperly?
deck.brief: Where should Lumen invest next to hold its lead over Quill and Paperly?
deck.answer: Lumen should invest next in retention and conversion: its new onboarding, now given to every signup, keeps 37% of August signups to March against Quill's 31%, and paying users nearly quadrupled in eight months; integrations, its widest gap, are tested before they are funded.

pages.highlight: conversion is the second lever to fund
points: Lumen's lead rests on retention, and only since its new onboarding: in a randomised August test it kept {{p-retention/new-onboarding@Mar 2026 | 0%}} of signups to March against {{p-retention/old-onboarding@Mar 2026 | 0%}} on the old one. Every signup has had it since September, so the lead over Quill now holds for the whole base.

Paying users nearly quadrupled in eight months and their share of actives more than doubled, at the highest price of the three, so conversion is the second lever to fund and price is not what holds it back.

Integrations are the widest gap, but nothing yet shows they cost users: measure retention by integration use before funding them. Paperly publishes no retention figure, so the lead is shown over Quill alone.

pages.title: Fund first-month retention and conversion now, and test integrations before matching rivals
items: Put the next retention money into the first month after signup, where the new onboarding still loses most of the users it loses.
Fund the conversion work that more than doubled the paying share of actives, and hold the price, which has not held conversion back.
Measure retention by integration use this quarter, and fund integrations only if users without them leave faster.
Treat the lead over Paperly as unproven until it publishes retention on the same basis as Lumen and Quill.
